neighbours.label: subject pronoun (they/he/it) of a subordinate clause when two earlier nouns compete as its antecedent
fire: Hamlet stabs Polonius through the curtain because he believes the king is hiding there.
The Vikings raided the monasteries wherever they landed along the coast.
Nurses recommend gloves even for visitors with clean hands, because they do not stop every germ.
When the general asked the scout for a report, he claimed to have seen nothing.
The city awarded Siemens the tram contract as it was the only bidder with local workshops.
The teachers praised the pupils after they finished the long project.
Romeo kills Tybalt in the square because he is furious about the death of his friend.
The farmers sold their sheep to the traders before they left the valley.
quiet: Hamlet draws his sword in the dark because the curtain is moving.
The Vikings rested wherever they landed along the coast.
Nurses recommend gloves, because clean hands do not stop every germ.
When the report arrived, the general read the news in silence.
The tram contract went to the only bidder with local workshops.
The teachers went home after they finished the long project.
Romeo is furious about the death of his friend and fights in the square.
The farmers locked the barn before they left the valley.

notes: Card: ' they' x16 after because/as/wherever. Probes: one candidate ('The villagers refused the offer because they') 0.03; two candidates (settlers/tribes wherever they 0.86, Macbeth/Duncan because he 0.48, king/wizard, he 0.37). Three near misses keep the pronoun with a single candidate.
